subject: Limited-term consolidation with soft auto-extend option
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Planning: ACME renewal — limited-term consolidation + soft auto-extend

Team —

Quick sync on ACME (DEAL-ACME-2026-219). They like keeping a shorter committed term to align with their fiscal change but want predictable pricing and an option to extend without heavy reprocurement. I argued we can offer a 12-month consolidated term across all products with a "soft auto-extend" clause: after month 10 we auto-offer a 3-month extension at a pre-negotiated blended rate unless they opt out.

Key asks for the thread:
- Confirm acceptable ramp schedule (month-by-month vs quarterly top-ups) — ACME expects a staged ramp to full reserved capacity over 6 months.
- Legal: can we phrase soft auto-extend as a renewal offer vs auto-renew? Need compliance sign-off.
- Finance: does blended-rate extension materially change unit economics vs standard 12-month?

I've attached the latest SOW draft and a burn estimate. Please comment quickly; Jill is pushing to get procurement language this week.

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@acme.ai>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planning: ACME renewal — limited-term consolidation + soft auto-extend

Thanks, Irene — appreciate the clear framing. A couple quick reactions from our side:

1) Staged ramp: ACME prefers monthly ramp checkpoints tied to usage and a one-time ability to accelerate (we may hit peak earlier if project moves faster). Can you include an opt-in burst option for months 1-3 with agreed temporary overage pricing?

2) Auto-extend language: Procurement is wary of anything that feels like "automatic" renewal. If you can position it as a "pre-authorized renewal offer" that we must proactively accept (i.e., opt-in) that will be fine — we need explicit vendor acceptance in the clause.

3) Exit ladder: we need an early-exit schedule (percent refund/credit on unused committed tokens) for the first 6 months if the project is canceled.

I'll send ACME's redlines to you separately.

Best,
Jill
VP Product, Acme AI
jill.thompson@acme.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planning: ACME renewal — limited-term consolidation + soft auto-extend

Jill —
Appreciate the clarity. Short answers:
- Monthly ramp checkpoints with optional 1-3 month burst window: yes. We'll include a capped burst pool (e.g., up to 25% additional capacity) billed at a defined increment.
- Soft auto-extend framing: legal prefers "offer to extend at pre-agreed terms; customer must accept to activate" language (so not technically auto-renew). I'll loop Legal but we can use that as the customer-facing phrasing.
- Early-exit credits: Finance is open to a pro-rated credit schedule for unused committed tokens in months 1-6, decreasing over time (e.g., 80% in month 1 down to 20% in month 6). That preserves economics while giving ACME an out.

Irene/Marissa — I'm attaching a pricing annex we can combine with the SOW to make these elements explicit. David, please confirm blended-rate impact.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales

From: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planning: ACME renewal — limited-term consolidation + soft auto-extend

Team —

Quick finance read: a 12-month consolidated term with the proposed soft-extension offer (3 months at a blended +5% uplift vs list monthly commitment) keeps gross margin within acceptable bounds if the early-exit credit schedule tapers as proposed. The burst pool (25% at +25% rate) is fine short-term but we should cap overall exposure by adding a total annual overage ceiling tied to committed baseline.

Numbers attached in onboarding-burn-estimates.xlsx. I'll flag any changes to accounting recognition if legal requires a renewal language that implies automatic continuation — we may need to treat the extension as a separate future contract for revenue recognition.

-David
David Kim
Finance Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@acme.ai>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planning: ACME renewal — limited-term consolidation + soft auto-extend

Thanks everyone — that all helps. Attached our redlines (ACME-redlines.docx). A couple of procurement asks to close before we route to Legal:

- Please replace any phrasing that reads as "automatic renewal" with "pre-authorized renewal offer" and include an explicit 30-day notification window for the customer to accept or decline.
- Early-exit credit: we request a minimum 70% protection for month 1, then sliding 70->30 over month 1-6. You propose 80->20; can we meet on 75->25?
- For the burst pool, please confirm surge ceiling per fiscal year (we propose 50% of baseline committed tokens).

If you can send a revised SOW and a clean pricing annex that reflect the 30-day opt-in window, 75->25 early-exit ladder, and a 50% annual surge ceiling, procurement will move to Legal review tomorrow.

Thanks — look forward to the updated SOW.

Best,
Jill
Jill Thompson
VP Product, Acme AI
